sources.title: Lynn Thorndike, The History of Medieval Europe (1917), chapter XXVII, printed pp. 511–530
sources.scope_note: User-supplied scan/OCR; chapter extract and hash retained in provenance. Broad sequence and institutions only. Dated judgments, racial/national generalizations, exact force totals, the Black Prince nickname explanation and simplified treaty renunciations are not adopted.

sources.title: Edward III, Royal Household
sources.scope_note: Reign and principal campaigns only; not rounded force, population, economic or casualty claims.

sources.title: Richard II, Royal Household
sources.scope_note: Succession, deposition and peace policy only; disputed death circumstances are not resolved.

sources.title: Henry IV, Royal Household
sources.scope_note: Kingship, Welsh revolt and Percy opposition only. Do not import every chronological detail of this overview.

sources.title: Henry V, Royal Household
sources.scope_note: Kingship and campaigns, not Shakespearean characterization or free institutional authority.

sources.title: Henry VI, Royal Household
sources.scope_note: Minority, dual-monarchy claim, Bedford and Normandy only; very large battle/casualty figures on the page are excluded.

sources.title: Grandes Chroniques de France, Library of Congress catalogue
sources.scope_note: Catalogue independently identifies Philip VI, John II and Charles V and their reigns. Manuscript partisanship is retained.

sources.title: Charles V authority record, Bibliothèque nationale de France
sources.scope_note: Identification and reign 1364–1380; the birth date is not needed to generate a skill or personal history.

sources.title: Malestroit, regional heritage inventory
sources.scope_note: Supports the 1343 truce and local commercial context; later buildings are not projected backward.

sources.title: Jean dit de Montfort, Institut culturel de Bretagne
sources.scope_note: Distinguishes the older claimant captured in 1341 from his son. No automatic inherited personal control.

sources.title: Auray au fil des siècles, municipal archives and heritage
sources.scope_note: Supports the 1364 battle and rival claimants, separately from the 1365 settlement.

sources.title: British Library Add MS 48004, transfer and renunciation documents
sources.scope_note: Catalogue evidence that territorial delivery and renunciation required further instruments; not instantaneous complete transfer.

sources.title: History of government: Anglo-Portuguese treaties
sources.scope_note: 1373 London treaty (TNA E30/275), 1385 crisis and separate 1386 Windsor instrument; no automatic present-day alliance behavior.

sources.title: Records of the Parliaments of Scotland, ordinance concerning the French army
sources.scope_note: Edited contemporary ordinance: joint command, supply and protection of sellers in the 1385 expedition. Prescribed conduct is not proof of compliance.

sources.title: Richard II treasure project timeline, Institute of Historical Research
sources.scope_note: 1396 diplomacy, 1399 deposition and 1400 death; treasure descriptions do not initialize present stocks.

sources.title: Cadw, Owain Glyndwr interpretation plan
sources.scope_note: Welsh revolt, French diplomacy and later intervention. The 1404 alliance and 1405 expedition cannot be installed in 1403.

sources.title: Sigilla/IRHT, Charles VI ratification of the Treaty of Troyes, TRA14200001/002
sources.scope_note: Document dated 21 May 1420. Treaty claims do not establish universal obedience.

sources.title: Loiret heritage, Sur les pas de Jeanne
sources.scope_note: Orléans and Loire campaign and Reims coronation in 1429; not evidence of every later location or military capacity.

sources.title: Treaty of Arras, Institut de France record via FranceArchives
sources.scope_note: Archival treaty identification, September 1435; territorial terms, delivery and personal adherence remain distinct.

sources.title: La Rochelle, Place de Verdun, Archéologie médiévale 26 (1996)
sources.scope_note: Historical/archaeological evidence for recovery of La Rochelle in 1372; no extrapolated modern street map.

sources.title: Froissart, edited Chronicles VIII.1, apparatus on the Bruges truce
sources.scope_note: Edited chronicle and apparatus: 1375 truce, prisoners and negotiations. Attributed medieval narrative, not neutral census.

sources.title: Castillon-la-Bataille municipal history
sources.scope_note: 1453 battle and Talbot. Modern commemorative performances are not historical troops; claims that feudalism simply ended are rejected.

sources.title: The National Archives, plague and labour legislation
sources.scope_note: 1349 ordinance and 1351 statute; legal attempts to constrain wages and movement are not measured compliance or market prices.

sources.title: The Soldier in Later Medieval England, soldiers named Large in Lancastrian Normandy
sources.scope_note: Documentary pay expectations for the described service: archer 6d, mounted man-at-arms 12d, foot man-at-arms 8d per day. No paid wage or universal rate inferred.

sources.title: Agincourt 600, 27 April–3 May 1415 military indentures
sources.scope_note: 1415 northern-France contract rates, 12d man-at-arms and 6d archer; rank, theatre, promised service and receipt remain separate.

sources.title: La Stabilisation de la monnaie par la création du franc (décembre 1360), Traditio
sources.scope_note: Scholarly abstract supports the 5 December ordinance and ransom/coinage context. Full article not acquired; no modern currency conversion or fixed exchange.

sources.title: The Great Schism, New Cambridge Medieval History chapter 20
sources.scope_note: Institutional papal schism context. Obedience, practice and individual affiliation remain separate; no automatic religion transfer.

sources.title: Records of the Parliaments of Scotland, historical introduction
sources.scope_note: David II’s release in 1357 and the subsequent ransom problem; a financial obligation is not a paid balance.

sources.title: Gascon Rolls Project, C61/101 calendar
sources.scope_note: Edited archival calendar records the 1389 truce and breaches by routiers. Its July date differs from the June date in some treaty summaries; no disputed exact signing day is adopted.

sources.title: The National Archives, medieval and early modern soldiers
sources.scope_note: Musters, accounts, retinues and treaty-roll research; an indexed name is not proof of current presence, loyalty or readiness.

sources.title: The National Archives, Jews in England in 1290
sources.scope_note: Edited letters establish discriminatory restrictions. Royal accusations are attributed hostile assertions, not facts about Jewish people. No absence, genetics or individual conduct is inferred.

sources.title: The use of English: Language, law, and political culture in fourteenth-century England, University of York
sources.scope_note: Scholarly abstract on the 1362 statute and continued French/English legal usage; no instant universal language change.

sources.title: Nelson H. Minnich, Great Western Schism, Pontifical Committee for Historical Sciences
sources.scope_note: Council depositions and Martin V’s November 1417 election; the late-1417 opening must reflect this change. Institutional recognition is not individual belief.

sources.title: Henry VI, Historic Royal Palaces
sources.scope_note: Summer 1453 incapacity and continuing kingship. Used only to withhold unsupported voluntary player control at the late-1453 cutoff; no retrospective diagnosis, predetermined recovery or public knowledge is installed.

sources.title: Century of Conflict opening and evidence policy, 21 October 2026
sources.scope_note: Authored cutoff, eligibility, qualitative scenario pressures and conditional requirements are design choices, not historical discoveries.

events.title: The War Begins
events.description: Edward III and Philip VI are in open conflict over Aquitaine and contested royal rights.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Edward III and Philip VI are in open conflict over Aquitaine and contested royal rights.

events.title: The Flemish Alliance
events.description: Sluys and the unsuccessful siege of Tournai have preceded the September truce at Esplechin.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Sluys and the unsuccessful siege of Tournai have preceded the September truce at Esplechin.

events.title: The Breton Succession
events.description: The death of Brittany's duke has opened competing Montfort and Penthièvre–Blois claims; the older John of Montfort has been captured.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The death of Brittany's duke has opened competing Montfort and Penthièvre–Blois claims; the older John of Montfort has been captured.

events.title: The Truce of Malestroit
events.description: The Malestroit truce has interrupted royal campaigning without settling the Breton succession.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The Malestroit truce has interrupted royal campaigning without settling the Breton succession.

events.title: The War Rekindled
events.description: English operations in Gascony have resumed; Henry of Grosmont's campaign has altered the military situation.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: English operations in Gascony have resumed; Henry of Grosmont's campaign has altered the military situation.

events.title: Scotland Enters the Campaign
events.description: Crécy and Neville's Cross have already occurred. David II is a captive; the siege of Calais continues.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Crécy and Neville's Cross have already occurred. David II is a captive; the siege of Calais continues.

events.title: The Truce of Calais
events.description: Calais has surrendered and a renewed truce follows; occupation and settlement now require administration.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Calais has surrendered and a renewed truce follows; occupation and settlement now require administration.

events.title: The Black Prince’s Campaign
events.description: Edward of Woodstock has conducted a destructive raid from Gascony into southern France.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Edward of Woodstock has conducted a destructive raid from Gascony into southern France.

events.title: The Captive King
events.description: John II has been captured at Poitiers. The dauphin Charles must conduct government amid a severe crisis.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: John II has been captured at Poitiers. The dauphin Charles must conduct government amid a severe crisis.

events.title: The Truces of Bordeaux and Berwick
events.description: John II remains captive while French government and the Parisian reform movement contest authority.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: John II remains captive while French government and the Parisian reform movement contest authority.

events.title: Edward’s Final Edwardian Offensive
events.description: Rejected peace terms have been followed by Edward III's new expedition toward Reims.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Rejected peace terms have been followed by Edward III's new expedition toward Reims.

events.title: The Peace of Brétigny
events.description: Brétigny and the subsequent Calais settlement have established terms for peace and John II's release.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Brétigny and the subsequent Calais settlement have established terms for peace and John II's release.

events.title: The Breton Settlement
events.description: Charles V is king of France. At Auray Charles of Blois has died and the younger John of Montfort has prevailed.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Charles V is king of France. At Auray Charles of Blois has died and the younger John of Montfort has prevailed.

events.title: The Castilian Civil War
events.description: Henry of Trastámara's intervention has displaced Pedro from much of Castile; the crown remains contested.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry of Trastámara's intervention has displaced Pedro from much of Castile; the crown remains contested.

events.title: The Caroline War
events.description: Charles V has renewed the Anglo-French war; Henry of Trastámara has defeated Pedro in Castile.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Charles V has renewed the Anglo-French war; Henry of Trastámara has defeated Pedro in Castile.

events.title: The Castilian Intervention
events.description: Castilian naval success at La Rochelle has damaged the English position; the town has returned to French authority.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Castilian naval success at La Rochelle has damaged the English position; the town has returned to French authority.

events.title: The Portuguese Connection
events.description: John of Gaunt's long expedition is crossing France without resolving the war.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: John of Gaunt's long expedition is crossing France without resolving the war.

events.title: The Truce of Bruges
events.description: French territorial recovery has narrowed England's position and a truce has been negotiated at Bruges.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: French territorial recovery has narrowed England's position and a truce has been negotiated at Bruges.

events.title: The War Resumes
events.description: Edward III has died and Richard II is king; renewed fighting and coastal attacks complicate the transition.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Edward III has died and Richard II is king; renewed fighting and coastal attacks complicate the transition.

events.title: The Scottish and Portuguese Fronts
events.description: A Franco-Scottish expedition has operated against England; Portugal's victory at Aljubarrota has strengthened John I.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: A Franco-Scottish expedition has operated against England; Portugal's victory at Aljubarrota has strengthened John I.

events.title: The Truce of Leulinghem
events.description: Richard II and Charles VI remain the reigning kings as the Leulinghem truce opens a longer diplomatic interval.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Richard II and Charles VI remain the reigning kings as the Leulinghem truce opens a longer diplomatic interval.

events.title: The Great Diplomatic Settlement
events.description: Richard II's marriage diplomacy with Isabella of France has reinforced the long truce.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Richard II's marriage diplomacy with Isabella of France has reinforced the long truce.

events.title: The Lancastrian Accession
events.description: Henry IV has deposed Richard II and taken the English throne; Richard remains a living captive at this cutoff.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry IV has deposed Richard II and taken the English throne; Richard remains a living captive at this cutoff.

events.title: The Welsh Rebellion
events.description: Owain Glyndŵr's revolt challenges English rule in Wales while Henry IV seeks to secure his kingship.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Owain Glyndŵr's revolt challenges English rule in Wales while Henry IV seeks to secure his kingship.

events.title: The Welsh War and Channel Conflict
events.description: Henry IV has defeated the Percy rising at Shrewsbury; the Welsh conflict and maritime hostility continue.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry IV has defeated the Percy rising at Shrewsbury; the Welsh conflict and maritime hostility continue.

events.title: England and the French Civil War
events.description: English forces have intervened in support of Burgundian interests in the French civil struggle.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: English forces have intervened in support of Burgundian interests in the French civil struggle.

events.title: The Lancastrian Invasion
events.description: Henry V prepared a cross-Channel expedition in 1415; subsequent events require their own evidence.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry V prepared a cross-Channel expedition in 1415; subsequent events require their own evidence.

events.title: The Conquest of Normandy
events.description: Henry V's renewed expedition has begun a sustained conquest in Normandy; Caen has fallen.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry V's renewed expedition has begun a sustained conquest in Normandy; Caen has fallen.

events.title: The Burgundian Alliance
events.description: Rouen has surrendered and John the Fearless has been killed at Montereau; Philip the Good succeeds in Burgundy.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Rouen has surrendered and John the Fearless has been killed at Montereau; Philip the Good succeeds in Burgundy.

events.title: The Treaty of Troyes
events.description: The Treaty of Troyes designates Henry V as heir and regent while Charles VI remains king; opposition continues.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The Treaty of Troyes designates Henry V as heir and regent while Charles VI remains king; opposition continues.

events.title: The Rival Monarchies
events.description: Henry V and Charles VI have died. Henry VI is an infant king, while Charles VII maintains a rival French kingship.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Henry V and Charles VI have died. Henry VI is an infant king, while Charles VII maintains a rival French kingship.

events.title: The French Resurgence
events.description: Orléans has been relieved and Charles VII crowned at Reims; the attempted recovery of Paris has not succeeded.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Orléans has been relieved and Charles VII crowned at Reims; the attempted recovery of Paris has not succeeded.

events.title: The Burgundian Reconciliation
events.description: The Arras settlement has reconciled Philip the Good with Charles VII; Bedford has died.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The Arras settlement has reconciled Philip the Good with Charles VII; Bedford has died.

events.title: The Truce of Tours
events.description: The Tours truce has interrupted major Anglo-French campaigning and marriage negotiations concern Margaret of Anjou.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The Tours truce has interrupted major Anglo-French campaigning and marriage negotiations concern Margaret of Anjou.

events.title: The Final War
events.description: The seizure of Fougères has helped break the truce; French and Breton operations have recovered Rouen.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: The seizure of Fougères has helped break the truce; French and Breton operations have recovered Rouen.

events.title: The Fall of English Normandy
events.description: Formigny and the surrender of Cherbourg have completed the collapse of English rule in Normandy.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Formigny and the surrender of Cherbourg have completed the collapse of English rule in Normandy.

events.title: The Fall of Bordeaux
events.description: Castillon and the recovery of Bordeaux have ended this historical sequence of major campaigning; Talbot is dead.

historical_outcome_reference.statement: Castillon and the recovery of Bordeaux have ended this historical sequence of major campaigning; Talbot is dead.

note: Year windows are research references, not occurrence dates or schedules. Conditions require separate actual evidence and are not an exhaustive causal model. No arbitrary chain makes one historical outcome a prerequisite of all later events. Future personal deaths and campaign termination are never executed.
